name: How does removing an acrylic shower compare to removing a tiled shower?

mainEntity.name: How does removing an acrylic shower compare to removing a tiled shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: Removing a fiberglass or acrylic unit involves cutting the insert into manageable sections with reciprocating saws, which creates less dust and removes quickly. In contrast, demolishing a custom tiled shower requires breaking up wall tiles, backer boards, and a dense mortar bed or mud pan, which is labor-intensive and produces significant masonry debris. While acrylic comes out cleanly in hours, tile tear-outs require extensive dust barriers, heavier hauling logistics, and closer inspection of studs that may have absorbed prolonged moisture.
acceptedAnswer.description: Acrylic units are cut and removed quickly with minimal mess. Tiled showers require breaking up dense mortar beds and tile, creating more heavy debris and dust.
